forms.name: Systems onboarding — the full audit
forms.description: The A-to-Z survey for a website + GoHighLevel + community engagement. Lists everything a client with zero assets would need; `satisfiedBy` removes whatever we already know, and whatever comes back empty is the work order.

fields.label: Your Google Business listing
fields.help: Search your business on Google and copy the link. It saves you typing your address, hours and phone, and it tells us what a customer sees before they ever reach your site.

fields.label: Where you are based
fields.help: Or the areas you cover, if customers do not come to you.

fields.label: What email do you actually use for the business?
fields.help: This matters more than it sounds. Google Workspace connects to your calendar, your customer records and your review requests with nothing in between. The others each need a workaround, and it is better to know now than to find out in week three.
options: Whatever came with my website host
Something else / I am not sure

fields.label: Which addresses are in use, and who reads them?
fields.help: info@, the owner's personal one, an old one nobody checks — all of it. We need to know where a lead currently lands.
fields.placeholder:
info@ — goes to me
bookings@ — nobody has checked it in a year

fields.label: Your website today
fields.help: Whatever you have, including nothing. We would rather tune up something decent than replace it for the sake of it.
options: Yes, and I am happy with it

fields.label: What is it built on, if you know?
fields.help: Wix, Squarespace, WordPress, GoDaddy, a guy who has stopped answering. Not knowing is a normal answer.

fields.label: Where is your domain name registered, and can you log in?
fields.help: GoDaddy, Namecheap, Google Domains, or whoever set it up. This is the single most common thing a business cannot get back into, and it is the one thing we cannot do without.

fields.label: How do you keep track of customers and follow-ups right now?
fields.help: Be honest — a notebook and your memory is the most common answer we get, and it is not a problem. We just need to know what we are moving from.
options: Nothing formal — my phone and my memory

fields.label: If you named one, which and how long?
If you already have one — keep it or move?
fields.help: No wrong answer. What decides it is whether it will talk to the new website: some connect cleanly, some only through a middleman, and a couple not at all. If you are happy where you are we will tell you honestly whether it can carry what you want it to do.
options: I do not have one — build me one
Keep what I have if it works with the site
Move me to whatever works best

fields.label: Do you want texts, reminders and follow-up going out automatically?
fields.help: Almost everyone says yes, and it is worth asking plainly because the answer decides the next four questions. Anything that texts a customer has to be registered with the phone carriers first, and that registration is the longest wait in the whole build — so we start it on day one.

fields.label: Your exact legal business name
fields.help: Not the sign on the door — the name on your registration, character for character, including the LLC or Inc. The phone companies check it against public records, and one wrong character sends the whole thing back to the start of a queue that takes weeks.

fields.label: And the name customers actually know you by, if it differs
fields.help: The DBA or trading name. Both can be registered; they just have to be declared honestly.

fields.label: EIN or Tax ID
fields.help: The federal number on your tax filings. A sole trader without one can still register — say so and we will use the route that fits. ⛔ Nobody else sees this; it goes to the carrier registration and nowhere else.

fields.label: The address on the registration
fields.help: Where the business is legally registered, which is often not where you work from. This has to match the record too.

fields.label: Who can sign for the business?
fields.help: Name, title and email of the person the carriers can verify. Usually you.

fields.label: Your customer list
fields.help: Everyone who has ever bought or enquired. Export it however it comes out — a CSV, a spreadsheet, a screenshot of your contacts. Names you already paid for are the fastest money in the whole engagement, and most people are sitting on more of them than they think.

fields.label: Which social accounts exist? Tick everything, even the abandoned ones.
fields.help: Nothing is a fine answer. We are not judging the accounts — we are deciding which ones get pointed at the new site and which ones we leave alone.

fields.label: Paste the links to the ones that matter
Have you ever run paid ads?
fields.help: If there is an old Meta or Google ad account, it usually still holds the audience and the history — worth recovering rather than starting cold.
options: Someone ran them for me and I do not know what happened to the account

fields.label: How do you get reviews at the moment?
fields.help: Almost everyone says 'when I remember'. That is the honest answer and it is the one we are here to fix.
options: I have a system that asks automatically

fields.label: How do you take money today?
fields.help: It decides what we can wire the booking and the coaching platform into without you changing banks.

fields.label: Are you running, or planning, a course, membership or coaching program?
fields.help: If not, say no and skip the next few — this whole section only applies to people selling what they know.

fields.label: Where does it live today?
fields.help: Skool, Kajabi, Teachable, a Facebook group, a shared Drive folder, nowhere yet. A Facebook group you do not own is the most common answer and the one worth moving.

fields.label: What is the program and what does it cost?
fields.help: In your words. The price matters because it sets what the funnel around it has to do.

fields.label: Upload whatever exists of it
fields.help: Slides, a curriculum, recorded calls, a rough outline on a napkin. Half-finished is normal.

fields.label: Do you have an email list, and where?
fields.help: Mailchimp, ConvertKit, a spreadsheet, the contacts in your phone. Size does not matter here — ownership does.

fields.label: Your logo, in the best quality you have
fields.help: If someone designed it, ask them for the original file — a version off your website is a photograph of a logo, not the logo. If you have never had one, say so; that is a job, not a problem.

fields.label: Brand colours and fonts, if they were ever decided
fields.placeholder: Navy and gold. Or: nobody ever decided.

fields.label: Photos of your own work, your team, your place
fields.help: Ten or so is plenty to start. Straight off your phone is fine — we resize and clean them up at our end. Real photos of your own work beat anything we could buy, every time.

fields.label: Any video at all?
fields.help: Phone footage counts. A wide clip cannot be cropped into a phone-shaped one, so if you are shooting new material, shoot it upright as well.

fields.label: What laptop or desktop do you actually work on?
fields.help: We are going to install things you use every day, and some of it behaves differently on a Mac than on a Windows machine. Easier to plan around your setup now than to hand you something that fights it.

fields.label: And your phone?
fields.help: The apps differ, the notifications differ, and how a booking reaches you differs. It is a thirty-second question that saves a support call.

fields.label: How do you feel about all this?
fields.help: There is no wrong answer and it changes how we hand things over, not what we build.
options: I would rather never touch it — just make it work

fields.label: Who else touches any of this?
fields.help: An office manager, a nephew who built the site, an agency still running your ads. We need to know who we will be coordinating with — or replacing.

fields.label: Who answers the phone and the messages today?
fields.help: This is the seat we are most often filling, so it helps to know whether it is you at nine at night.

fields.label: Why do customers pick you over the other guy?
fields.help: In your own words. Do not polish it — I would rather have how you would say it out loud.

fields.label: What is the one thing that, if it just worked, would change your month?

forms.note: These questions go deeper than you are used to, and there is a reason. Your tools have to work together, and they do not all play nicely with each other — the email you use decides what your calendar can do, and the phone in your pocket decides what we can install. Twenty minutes here saves a month of surprises. Wherever the answer is 'nothing', say nothing. That is useful too.
forms.successBody: Now we know exactly what you have and what is missing, which means the plan we come back with is built on your actual setup rather than a guess. Nothing you left blank is a problem; the blanks are simply the list of what we build first.
